  f <- file.path(ROOT, p)
  if (!file.exists(f)) { MISSING <<- c(MISSING, p); return(NULL) }

# The question, and the one-paragraph answer

**IB1** is a composite lymph node from one patient: classic Hodgkin lymphoma together with
follicular lymphoma. **RB1** is the FL recurrence from the same patient — the same clone, no
Hodgkin component. Steps 07–12 localised the two diseases *inside* IB1 and used RB1 only as a
whole-sample null. This step asks the obvious next question: **does the FL look different when
it sits next to a Hodgkin field?**

<div class="verdict-no">
**The direct comparison is not identifiable, and that is the first result.** IB1's FL foci and
RB1's follicles do not overlap in cell composition: matching 100 µm bins on B-cell share,
depth, cell count and typability matched **2 of 44**. IB1's *most* B-dense quartile is less
B-rich than RB1's *least* B-dense quartile. Any unmatched cross-sample contrast measures cell
mix, not FL biology — and a difference-in-differences does not rescue it, because the two
reference tissues differ too.
</div>

<div class="verdict-ok">
**What the data does support**, once the unit is changed from tissue to cell type, to region, or
to arrangement: a Hodgkin chemokine field that grades into IB1's B-dense tissue and carries
BATF3/CD40/IL6 with it; a CCR4 gradient without a Treg signature; Tfh as the PD-1 source in
both nodes; a spatially structured IB1 node against a spatially homogeneous RB1; and a clean
negative on PD-1/PD-L1 itself.
</div>

# What was built

```{r built}
b <- data.table(
  Stage = c("16a regions","16b cell types","16c matching","16d bin DE","16j/16m cell-type DE",
            "16k composition","16g field gradient","16h co-occurrence","16r FL-edge rings",
            "16e checkpoint","16n Tfh figures"),
  Question = c("region label per cell, both samples",
               "cross-sample-comparable cell types incl. Tfh",
               "can FL territory be matched across samples?",
               "region-unit DE, bin as the unit",
               "DE conditioned on cell type",
               "composition, and enrichment ratios",
               "does the Hodgkin field grade into nearby tissue?",
               "is the same cell mix arranged differently?",
               "expression across the FL boundary",
               "PD-1 / PD-L1 / PD-L2 in detail",
               "what is a Tfh cell here?"),
  Verdict = c("built and validated","validated on held-out markers","**FAILED — the result**",
              "C1/C2/C5 sound; C3/C4 retracted","the fix for identifiability",
              "needed two corrections","**strongest positive**","**organisational difference**",
              "dose-response in both nodes","**mostly negative**","Tfh validated, Treg not"))
tbl(b, "Every stage ran on both QC tiers unless noted. Results are reported only where the two tiers agree.")
```

<details>
<summary>The two QC tiers, and why a symmetric one had to be built</summary>

IB1 lost **2,013,225** cells to a staining/section rule that RB1 was never evaluated for
(`qc_spatial_staining == "not_evaluated"`, `fail_staining = 0`). The existing pools are
therefore asymmetrically filtered, and every published cross-sample number inherits that.

- **`matched`** (primary) — `qc_spatial_fovpx == "ok" & qcCellsPassed`, ignoring staining
  entirely: **IB1 1,877,697 / RB1 1,399,189**. Same rules both samples; IB1 is the *larger*
  pool. Cluster `i` (over-fixation) is then dropped per cell, leaving 767,395 / 1,286,223.
- **`strict`** (sensitivity) — the existing `qc_passing_all` pools, which after the cluster-`i`
  drop reproduce `output/10_hrs/hrs_segments.csv.gz` exactly (251,747 / 1,286,223).

The symmetric tier also settles something step 13 lists as FAILED. At the matched tier IB1 has
**80 chemokine hotspots (66 seam-free)** and **zero RB1 bins clear the same cut** — the
pre-QC-symmetric negative control the project previously lacked.
</details>

# Regions, and whether RB1 can be regionalised at all

RB1's light-chain readout is degenerate: 178 of 178 neighbourhoods are kappa-restricted and
1,276,791 of 1,286,223 cells sit inside one. Clonality cannot partition it. The axis that can is
**architecture** — per-100 µm-bin B-cell share among *lineage-assigned* cells, thresholded on
within-sample quantiles so the two nodes are compared on rank rather than on absolute
composition.

<details>
<summary>Why the denominator matters, and a correction made along the way</summary>

The first version called architecture on raw `f_B` and its own diagnostic rejected it:
`B_sparse` came out **lineage-negative** dominated in both samples (median unassigned fraction
0.21 in RB1, 0.36 in IB1) while the T fraction barely moved. "B-poor" was tracking how much of a
bin could be typed at all. Renormalising to the assignable cells removed the confound and then
the classes separated properly — and exposed an asymmetry:

- **RB1's B-poor tissue is a genuine T-zone**: T share among assigned rises 2.07×, myeloid 5.09×.
- **IB1's is myeloid-rich and T-*depleted***: T share 0.53×, myeloid 1.86×.

So "interfollicular" is supported in RB1 and **not** in IB1. The two nodes' non-follicular tissue
is different tissue, which is what later sank the difference-in-differences.
</details>

`B_dense` passes a spatial-coherence permutation in both samples (p = 0.005), and in IB1 — where
an independent clonality-based FL call exists — it recovers **72–77%** of the light-chain-defined
FL cells. That is the justification for using it on RB1.

```{r regions-fig, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Disease regions and the shared architecture axis. RB1 shows follicle-scale B_dense patches with an interconnected interfollicular network; IB1's post-QC tissue is fragmented and its FL foci are small and few."}
imgt("output/16_regions/%s/figures/fig_16_regions_RB1.png")
imgt("output/16_regions/%s/figures/fig_16_regions_IB1.png")
```

## How much of the section the QC removes

The maps above are the primary (`matched`) tier. Running the identical region builder with **no
spatial QC at all** shows what the filter costs in coverage — and it is not subtle.

```{r preqc-fig, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Pre-QC: the same region builder over all 4,406,940 segmented cells. IB1 resolves into two complete tissue pieces with follicle-scale B_dense structure across both. The fragmentation visible in the post-QC map above is the filter, not the tissue."}
img("output/16_regions/preqc/figures/fig_16_regions_IB1.png")
```

```{r preqc-tab}
a <- rd("output/16_regions/preqc/bin_region_summary.csv")
b <- rdt("output/16_regions/%s/bin_region_summary.csv")
if (!is.null(a) && !is.null(b)) {
  a[, tier := "preqc"]; b[, tier := TIER]
  tbl(rbind(a, b, fill = TRUE)[samp == "IB1"][order(bin_region, tier)][
        , .(tier, bin_region, bins, cells, fovs, med_depth)],
      "IB1 coverage, pre-QC against the primary tier. FL_focus goes from 89 bins in 23 FOVs to 102 in 26, and all 976 light-chain FL member cells survive pre-QC against 45.4% at the strict tier.")
}
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**Pre-QC is for POSITION, not magnitude.** Step 11 established that the spatial filter discards
cells carrying *more* chemokine than it keeps, so a pre-QC cp10k is not comparable to a post-QC
one, and RB1's staining flag is `not_evaluated` so the cross-sample control cannot follow either.
The pre-QC tier derives its own thresholds (hotspot cut 177.8 cp10k against 176.1 matched, 120.9
strict) and they must not be compared across tiers. IB1 is 59% over-fixation cluster `i` pre-QC,
dropped per cell as always. Use these maps to see where things are; use the matched tier for
every number.
</div>

```{r region-summary}
tbl(rdt("output/16_regions/%s/bin_region_summary.csv"),
    "Bin-level regions, the unit of every region test below. IB1's FL_focus is 89 bins across 23 FOVs at the matched tier — against 44 across 9 at the strict tier, which is why the symmetric tier matters for power and not only for fairness.")
```

# The comparison that cannot be made

```{r matching}
tbl(rdt("output/16_matched/%s/matched_summary.csv"),
    "Cross-sample bin matching on B share, log cell count, log depth and typability. Balance is achieved where matching succeeds (worst |SMD| < 0.11) — the failure is coverage, not balance.")
tbl(rdt("output/16_matched/%s/matched_balance.csv")[grepl("^FL", group)],
    "The FL pairing in detail. The pre-matching standardised mean difference on fb_a is 4.6 standard deviations.")
```

```{r matching-fig, out.width="70%", fig.cap="Standardised mean differences before and after matching. The reference groups match; the FL groups do not, because there is no overlap to match on."}
imgt("output/16_matched/%s/figures/fig_16_matching_balance.png")
```

<div class="verdict-no">
**2 of 89 IB1 FL bins found a composition-matched RB1 partner** (2 of 44 at the strict tier).
The cleanest statement of why: IB1's most B-dense quartile has a B share among typed cells of
**0.286**, and RB1's least B-dense quartile has **0.484**. The distributions are disjoint. The
recurrence has effaced the node so completely that no part of it is as B-poor as the B-richest
part of the composite node.
</div>

## Two contrasts that were retracted

**C3, the unmatched cross-sample FL contrast.** Its top genes — CCL19 +3.59, CCL21 +2.95,
LYZ +3.12, APOE +3.67, PTGDS +2.67 — are precisely the genes that mark RB1's *interfollicular*
zone in C2. It was measuring that IB1's FL bins are 17.6% B cells sitting in a myeloid-rich node
while RB1's follicular bins are 50.9% B. Reported as an effect size only.

**C4, the difference-in-differences.** Intended as the primary result, on the reasoning that a
per-sample technical shift cancels. It returned the same gene list, because the two reference
groups are also different tissue (above). Subtracting a T-zone-referenced contrast from a
myeloid-referenced one leaves the T-zone difference behind wearing a result's clothing. Its
bootstrap p also saturates at the floor for ~900 genes because it resamples bins, not FOVs.
**C4 is withdrawn, not reinterpreted.**

# Changing the unit: condition on cell type

A B cell is a B cell in either node, so conditioning on cell type removes composition by
construction rather than by matching — the move step 14 made when it tested expression within
each cluster instead of pooled.

```{r ctde}
d <- rdt("output/16_ct_de/%s/ct_de.csv.gz")
if (!is.null(d)) {
  s <- d[, .(genes_sig = sum(concordant & q < 0.05 & !is_selection),
             fov_robust = sum(concordant & q < 0.05 & !is_selection &
                              !is.na(q_fov) & q_fov < 0.05),
             n_a = n_a[1], n_b = n_b[1]), by = .(contrast, celltype)]
  tbl(s[order(contrast, celltype)],
      "Cell-type-conditioned DE. Test: Mann-Whitney U per gene, one observation per bin pseudobulk, BH-adjusted across genes within each contrast. `fov_robust` repeats the same test with bins collapsed to their FOV.")
}
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**93% of the apparent cross-sample B-cell difference was sequencing depth.** Matched, 251 genes;
unmatched, 2,894 — 2,693 lost to depth matching alone. Depth matching balanced every contrast
(worst SMD 1.48 → 0.01) at heavy cost in n (IB1 FL B cells: 80 → 27 bin-pseudobulks).
</div>

Two earlier results turn out to be **compositional rather than cell-state**:

- **IB1 FL focus vs IB1 background has zero significant genes within B or T cells.** The
  CXCL13/CLU/FCER2/IGHD signature reported at bin level is "more B cells present", not B cells
  behaving differently.
- **The BATF3 hotspot signal likewise vanishes within B and T** (myeloid: 2 genes). The cHL
  hotspot is a DC-rich *region*, not a state change — which matches step 11's own wording, now
  demonstrated rather than assumed. Note this does **not** mean BATF3 is absent regionally; see
  the field section, where it is the strongest gene in the phase.

What survives, both tiers, composition- and depth-free — IB1 FL vs RB1 follicular:

- **B cells**: IGHD +2.04, SELL +1.98 (naive/mantle) up in IB1; JCHAIN −2.62 (plasmacytic) down.
- **T cells**: LAG3 +1.99, CXCL13 +1.77, CTLA4 +0.70, TIGIT −0.65.
- **Myeloid**: CXCL9 −2.83.

<details>
<summary>A caveat on the B-cell signature</summary>
IGHD and SELL are naive/mantle markers. IB1's FL foci are focal within a largely non-FL node, so
they plausibly mix clone with residual normal mantle B cells — which would produce exactly this
signature. The result is reported; the alternative explanation is not excluded.
</details>

# Composition: what follows the FL B cells

```{r comp-fig, out.width="85%", fig.cap="Enrichment in FL territory relative to each sample's own B-cell enrichment. Tfh is the only population that follows the B cells to a comparable degree in both nodes."}
imgt("output/16_composition/%s/figures/fig_16_composition_did.png")
```

```{r comp}
tbl(rdt("output/16_composition/%s/enrichment_relative_to_B.csv")[
      grepl("architecture", pairing)][order(-rel_to_B_IB1)][, .(
      celltype, enrich_IB1, enrich_RB1, rel_to_B_IB1, rel_to_B_RB1, follows_B_ratio)],
    "Symmetric B_dense-vs-B_sparse definition, normalised to each sample's own B enrichment. Descriptive ratios of cell-type shares -- no test, so read the size and not a threshold.")
```

<details>
<summary>Why the raw difference-in-differences on composition also needed fixing</summary>
It came out positive for all 16 cell types under both region definitions — one scale artifact,
not 16 findings. IB1's `B_dense`-vs-`B_sparse` contrast spans a B share of 0.286 → 0.029 (~10×)
while RB1's spans 0.790 → 0.484 (~1.6×), because RB1 is uniformly B-rich. IB1's B enrichment is
therefore 17.99× against RB1's 1.65× before any other cell type is considered, and everything
inherits it. Dividing by the same-sample B enrichment removes it.
</details>

**Tfh is the only population that follows the FL B cells at a comparable rate in both nodes**
(0.465 IB1 / 0.416 RB1 of the B enrichment), leading the next population by 3–4× in each sample
independently. Rank and direction hold across tiers; the magnitude does not (ratio 1.12 matched,
1.52 strict), so the rank is the claim.

# The Hodgkin field, and what it does to nearby tissue

This is the strongest positive result, and it runs entirely inside IB1 — so it is immune to the
composition disjointness, the QC asymmetry and the depth difference all at once.

```{r c5}
d <- rdt("output/16_de/%s/de_contrasts.csv.gz")
if (!is.null(d)) tbl(head(d[contrast == "C5" & concordant & q < 0.05 & !is_selection][
      order(-abs(log2fc))][, .(gene, cp10k_hotspot = round(cp10k_a,2),
      cp10k_background = round(cp10k_b,2), log2fc = round(log2fc,2),
      det_log2 = round(log2fc_det,2), q = signif(q,2), q_fov = signif(q_fov,2))], 14),
  "cHL hotspot vs IB1 background, matched tier. Test: Mann-Whitney U per gene, one observation per bin pseudobulk, BH-adjusted across the whole panel; `q_fov` is the same test with FOV as the unit. 551 genes are significant and survive FOV collapse (222 at the strict tier). CCL17/CCL22 define the region and are excluded.")
```

BATF3 is tier-consistent and stronger at the matched tier: **+1.77 → +2.07 log2FC, q = 3e-37**,
FOV-robust in both. CD40 +0.92 and IL6 +1.31 likewise. These are step 10's Hodgkin-specific genes,
recovered from an independent construction.

## Is hotspot BATF3 real, or spillover from DCs?

Hotspots are DC-rich, and a BATF3-high cDC bleeding transcripts into its neighbours would raise
BATF3 in every adjacent cell regardless of type — at roughly the one-transcript-per-cell level
the data shows. Spillover and a field make opposite predictions about distance to the nearest cDC.

```{r batf3}
tbl(rd("output/16_checkpoint/batf3_spillover.csv")[, .(dband,
      n_hot = cells_cHL_hotspot, n_bg = cells_background,
      cp10k_hot = cp10k_cHL_hotspot, cp10k_bg = cp10k_background, ratio_cp10k,
      det_hot = pct_det_cHL_hotspot, det_bg = pct_det_background, ratio_det,
      depth_hot = med_depth_cHL_hotspot, depth_bg = med_depth_background)],
  "BATF3 in NON-cDC cells, hotspot vs background, by distance to the nearest cDC, depth-matched within decile. Descriptive: no test is run here -- the design decides between spillover and a field by the SHAPE of the ratio across distance bands, which a p-value on any single band would not capture.")
```

<div class="verdict-ok">
The ratio is **highest farthest from any cDC** (5.14× at >120 µm, detection agreeing at 3.08×),
which is the opposite of spillover decay. A real regional field, not a segmentation artifact.
</div>

## The CCR4 gradient

CCL17 and CCL22 signal through CCR4, which recruits Treg and Th2 cells. That was declared as the
readout **before** the genome-wide scan, so it cannot be a post-hoc pick from 6,175 genes.

```{r ccr4}
tbl(rdt("output/16_gradient/%s/ccr4_axis.csv")[, .(set, gene, bins, fovs,
      rho_field = round(rho_field,3), q_field = signif(q_field,2),
      rho_field_fov = round(rho_field_fov,3), is_selection)][order(set, -abs(rho_field))],
  "Test: Spearman's rho against the local CCL17+CCL22 field, one observation per bin, BH-adjusted across the gene set; `rho_field_fov` repeats it with FOV as the unit. Rank-based, so it needs monotonicity and not linearity. Hotspot bins are excluded from the response; CCL17/CCL22 define the exposure and are held out.")
```

```{r ccr4-fig, out.width="90%", fig.cap="The pre-declared genes against distance from the nearest hotspot. Only CCR4 and CTLA4 track the field; the Treg markers do not. Y-axes are free — read the span in each strip, not the slope."}
imgt("output/16_gradient/%s/figures/fig_16_field_gradient.png")
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**CCR4 rho = 0.415 inside FL foci** (q = 1.4e-4, and 0.431 across FOV means — robust at both
units), against 0.120 tissue-wide: the association is ~3.5× stronger in FL tissue. **But FOXP3 is
flat (rho −0.007, rank 2534/6175) and IL2RA is negatively associated.** This is a CCR4 gradient
**without** a Treg signature — Th2 or other CCR4⁺ cells, or CCR4 upregulation, not Treg
recruitment. It should not be reported as a Treg result.
</div>

Genome-wide, the field axis independently recovers the cHL programme: BATF3 0.555 and CD40 0.389
lead the positive list with IL6 0.335, while the negative list is the normal T-zone architecture
(CXCL12 −0.572, CCL21 −0.539, C1QA/B/C). 1,723 of 6,175 genes are field-associated at both units.

# Arrangement: the same cell mix, organised differently

Composition and expression are nearly exhausted as questions once the cell-type conditioning
shows most regional signal is compositional. What had not been asked is whether the same cell
types are *arranged* differently. The null permutes labels within local-density deciles, holding
composition and geometry fixed and randomising only the assignment of types to positions.

```{r cooccur-fig, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Mean type-b neighbours within 20 um of a type-a cell, against a density-matched null. 1.0 is exactly chance. Numbers shown where q < 0.05."}
imgt("output/16_cooccur/%s/figures/fig_16_cooccurrence.png")
```

```{r cooccur}
tbl(rdt("output/16_cooccur/%s/tfh_partners.csv")[, .(samp, bin_region, b,
      n_a, obs, null, enrich, q = signif(q,2))][order(samp, bin_region, -enrich)],
  "Tfh and its neighbours. Test: observed neighbour counts against a permutation null that reshuffles cell-type labels while holding local cell density fixed, one observation per neighbourhood, BH-adjusted. `enrich` is observed/null. RB1 sits at chance throughout; IB1 does not.")
```

<div class="verdict-ok">
**IB1's node is spatially structured; RB1's is not.** In IB1 background (best powered, q = 0.014
at both tiers) Tfh self-aggregate at **2.74×** chance, preferentially neighbour B cells at
**1.62×**, and avoid macrophages at **0.47×**; lymphocyte/myeloid segregation runs 0.48–0.57×
throughout. In RB1 essentially every pair sits at chance (0.93–1.09). Tfh–B in RB1 follicles is
9.82 observed against 9.89 expected — a Tfh there has ten B neighbours because the tissue is 51%
B, with no preferential pairing on top.
</div>

This is the one place where "differently organised" is demonstrated rather than inferred, because
the null holds composition fixed by construction. It also fits the effacement story: RB1's clone
has homogenised the node, IB1 retains architecture.

# Across the FL boundary

Rings replace step 14's binary in/out with a dose–response. At n = 1 a two-group p-value says two
arbitrary groups differ; a monotone gradient across seven bands is much harder to produce by
accident. The boundary is defined identically in both samples from the shared architecture axis,
and the unit is the FOV.

```{r rings-fig, out.width="95%", fig.cap="Expression across the B_dense (FL) boundary. Dashed line is the boundary; left of it is inside FL tissue."}
imgt("output/16_rings/%s/figures/fig_16_fl_edge_rings.png")
```

```{r rings}
d <- rdt("output/16_rings/%s/ring_trend_concordance.csv")
if (!is.null(d) && "both" %in% names(d))
  tbl(head(d[both == TRUE][order(-abs(med_rho_IB1))][, .(gene,
        IB1 = round(med_rho_IB1,3), RB1 = round(med_rho_RB1,3))], 12),
      "Genes edge-graded in both nodes, same direction (51 of 103; between-sample correlation of the trend 0.64). Test: Spearman's rho of expression against ring index within each FL-boundary neighbourhood, then the MEDIAN rho across neighbourhoods -- the neighbourhood is the replicate, not the ring. Negative = higher inside FL tissue.")
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**IB1's `B_dense` tissue is not FL-programme tissue, and this qualifies several results above.**
RB1's boundary grades the FL germinal-centre programme — BCL2 −0.70, BCL6 −0.70, MME/CD10 −0.74,
RGS13 −0.70, IGKC −0.83. In IB1 the same genes are flat (MME +0.10, BCL6 0.00, BCL2 −0.10,
RGS13 +0.14). IB1's B-dense tissue has B-cell markers but not the tumour programme.

What it has instead is the Hodgkin field: **CCL17 runs 21.8 → 7.3 and CCL22 11.4 → 3.3 across the
boundary in IB1, and both are flat in RB1** (~1.5, ~1.0), with CTLA4, LAG3 and CXCL13 doing the
same.

Consequence: any result computed on the shared `arch` axis — including the Tfh composition
finding — is about **B-dense tissue**, and the two nodes' B-dense tissue is different biology.
Results computed on the light-chain FL definition (the cell-type-conditioned contrasts, C1) are
genuinely about FL.
</div>

# PD-1, PD-L1 and PD-L2

<div class="verdict-mid">
**This section reports a negative. Step 17 was built to test whether that negative holds,
and it both strengthens and partly overturns what follows.** See
`output/17_summary/step17_PD1_PDL1.html`. In brief:

- The negative **holds** for the cross-sample comparison, and more strongly than stated
  here. A within-cell-type difference-in-differences against the two samples' reference
  zones leaves **0 of 30 gene x stratum combinations significant**; *CXCL13*'s cross-sample
  odds ratio of 5.21 deflates to 0.98 and *LAG3*'s 4.64 to 1.45. The between-slide offset
  for these genes is larger than any regional effect within either slide, which bounds the
  whole two-section design.
- The negative is **overturned within each sample**, where a per-cell binomial model with
  depth stratified out has power that the region-level rank tests here do not. IB1's Hodgkin
  hotspots carry elevated *CD274* (OR 1.74) and *PDCD1LG2* (OR 1.81) with *PDCD1* flat --
  ligand side only. RB1's follicles carry *PDCD1* in T cells at OR 1.82
  (*q* = 4.6 x 10^-14), the recognised follicular PD-1 pattern of FL.
- Step 17 also **retracts** its own sign-consistency result on the same grounds.
</div>

## What a "Tfh" cell is here

The label is a marker-argmax call, not a cluster: cells first called `T` on CD3D/E/G/TRAC, then
an argmax within them over {Tfh, Treg, CD8_T, CD4_conv}. **PDCD1 and CTLA4 are excluded from the
definition**, so the PD-1 readout is not circular.

```{r tfh-fig, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Marker profile by cell type and node. The HELD OUT block is the evidence: the call never saw PDCD1 or CTLA4."}
imgt("output/16_tfh/%s/figures/fig_16_tfh_markers_by_celltype.png")
```

```{r tfh-check}
tbl(rdt("output/16_tfh/%s/../../16_celltypes/celltype_holdout_check.csv"),
    "Rank among SIBLINGS on marker genes -- descriptive, no test. Only `genuinely_held_out` rows are evidence: a gene used to make the call cannot validate it.")
```

**Tfh is validated** — top sibling on held-out PDCD1 (2.49 cp10k, 1.19× the next). **Treg is
not** — rank 2 behind Tfh on CTLA4 (3.07 vs 3.26), so it has no independent validator on this
panel and is flagged weakly-supported wherever it appears. On this panel every myeloid and DC
marker is definitional, so Macrophage/cDC separation is descriptive, not validated.

```{r tfh-region-fig, out.width="100%", fig.cap="The Tfh profile is stable across regions: defining markers and held-out PDCD1 are elevated in the Tfh column of every regional category."}
imgt("output/16_tfh/%s/figures/fig_16_tfh_markers_by_region.png")
```

```{r tfh-views, out.width="100%", fig.cap="A representative Tfh cell in IB1's FL focus and in RB1's follicle. Panels: colorized image with slide locator, cell boundaries by type, and transcripts with PDCD1 in its own colour. Red box marks the same cell in all panels. Selection is a stated rule, not a hand-picked best case."}
imgt("output/16_tfh_views/%s/tfh_IB1_FL_focus_2_517_2780.png")
imgt("output/16_tfh_views/%s/tfh_RB1_FL_follicular_1_403_1370.png")
```

## The measurement floor, which bounds everything below

```{r negfloor}
tbl(rd("output/16_checkpoint/negprobe_verdict.csv")[gene %in%
      c("PDCD1","CD274","PDCD1LG2","CTLA4","LAG3","CXCL13","IGKC","CD3E","CD68")][, .(
      gene, rec_thr, pct_det_thr1_IB1, pct_det_at_rec_IB1, ratio_at_rec_IB1, ratio_at_rec_RB1)],
  "Detection against the mean blank probe. At >=1 count CD274 is 2.7x the blank rate; at >=2 the blank rate collapses to 0.05% and it is 25.8x. Every panel gene reaches >=10x specificity at >=2 counts.")
```

<details>
<summary>Depth predicts positivity at AUC ~0.70 for every gene, including the positive controls</summary>

IGKC — which is how the FL clone was *defined* — shows 0.693/0.733; CD3E 0.695/0.649; CD68
0.731/0.671; against PDCD1 0.711 and CD274 0.699. So **AUC ≈ 0.70 versus depth is a property of
thresholding a sparse count on this platform, not a signature of noise.** The consequence is that
depth matching is mandatory for any per-cell positivity comparison, which is done throughout.

Side note, not acted on: step 10 rejected per-cell CD30 partly on TNFRSF8's depth-AUC of 0.716,
which is indistinguishable from IGKC's. That closed avenue may deserve revisiting; CLAUDE.md
keeps it closed and this step did not reopen it.
</details>

## Where PD-1 lives, and what does not differ

```{r pd1}
d <- rdt("output/16_checkpoint/%s/checkpoint_pooled.csv")
if (!is.null(d)) tbl(dcast(d[gene == "PDCD1" & celltype %in% c("Tfh","Treg","CD4_conv","CD8_T",
      "T_unresolved","B","Macrophage","Monocyte","cDC")], celltype ~ samp + bin_region,
      value.var = "cp10k"),
  "PDCD1 cp10k by cell type and region. POOLED over cells — effect sizes, not tests. Tfh leads in every region of both nodes.")
```

**Tfh is the PD-1 source in both nodes** (3.78 in IB1 FL foci, 4.12 in RB1 follicles, against
1.0–2.8 for every other type), established independently of the call.

```{r pd1-test}
d <- rdt("output/16_checkpoint/%s/checkpoint_region_unit.csv")
if (!is.null(d)) tbl(d[gene %in% c("PDCD1","CD274","PDCD1LG2")][order(contrast, celltype, gene)][
      , .(contrast, celltype, gene, n_a, cp10k_a = round(cp10k_a,2),
          cp10k_b = round(cp10k_b,2), log2fc = round(log2fc,2), q = signif(q,2), concordant)],
  "The same three genes with the REGION as the unit, depth-matched, within cell type. Test: Mann-Whitney U on bin pseudobulks, BH-adjusted. Nothing reaches q < 0.05 -- see the power bound below before reading that as absence.")
```

<div class="verdict-no">
**PDCD1, CD274 and PDCD1LG2 differ nowhere** between regions within any cell type after depth
matching (all q ≥ 0.11), and the spatial PD-1→PD-L1 pairing shows **no reproducible engagement**:
every significant pairing result either flips between tiers or is a 0.7 µm effect on n = 7,182.
What *does* differ within T cells (both tiers, IB1 FL vs RB1 follicular) is LAG3 +1.99,
CTLA4 +0.70 and TIGIT −0.65, with CD80 −1.63 and CD86 −1.24 in B cells. The co-stimulation and
exhaustion landscape differs while PD-1/PD-L1 itself is flat.

At ~1–2% positivity this is a **floor result, not proof of absence** — a distinction that matters
if this reaches a checkpoint-blockade discussion.
</div>

```{r pairing}
tbl(rdt("output/16_checkpoint/%s/spatial_pairing.csv"),
    "PD-1+ to nearest ligand+ distance against a density- and cell-type-matched permutation null, one observation per region. ratio > 1 with p < 0.05 would mean closer than chance. The null holds cell density and composition fixed, so it tests ARRANGEMENT and not abundance.")
```

# What this step cannot support

```{r limits}
l <- data.table(
  Claim = c("IB1 FL vs RB1 FL, expression, at matched composition",
            "Difference-in-differences on expression",
            "Region-unit tests for Tfh, Treg, Macrophage, cDC",
            "Any statement about pDC",
            "Treg as a reliable label",
            "PD-1/PD-L1 axis is not engaged",
            "Results on the shared `arch` axis are about FL",
            "FL-edge ring trends, genome-wide",
            "Anything population-level"),
  Status = c("**not identifiable**","**withdrawn**","**not possible**","**not possible**",
             "**unsupported**","**floor result**","**qualified**","**not run**","**never**"),
  Why = c("2 of 89 bins match; the distributions are disjoint",
          "the two reference tissues differ, so nothing cancels",
          "under one cell per 100 um bin; pooled effect sizes only",
          "the two-stage call does not resolve it on this panel",
          "rank 2 behind Tfh on its only held-out marker",
          "~1-2% positivity; absence of evidence, not evidence of absence",
          "IB1's B_dense carries no FL programme (BCL2/BCL6/MME flat)",
          "rings ran on the 103-gene panel, not all 6,175",
          "n = 1 patient; everything here is descriptive"))
tbl(l, "Limits carried out of this step. The first two were intended as primary results.")
```
